blocks.text: TAIPEI – Taiwan President Lai Ching-te devoted most of his national day speech to domestic issues, but analysts saw his call for Taiwan to become a “city upon a hill”, a biblical image and a phrase long used by US politicians, as a message to Washington. After a morning of marching bands and mass displays, Lai took the podium in front of the presidential office building on Oct 10 to laud Taiwan’s achievements and mark the 30th anniversary of the island’s first direct presidential election.
